app.title: Crop Stress Prediction from Satellite Data (Streamlit app)
app.summary: A person picks one of two trained classifiers and sees its held-out test scores and tuned decision threshold, then narrows the sites to one group. A map shows each site's latest predicted stress, a site chosen from a list shows its vegetation index and predicted probability over time with a table of recent periods, and further tabs compare stress incidence, test performance and seasonal profiles across groups and count how many usable satellite readings each site actually had. Finally they pick one site and period and get a feature-by-feature breakdown of how the model reached that prediction, set against the threshold and the actual label.

task.text: Check a trained early-warning classifier's predictions of vegetation-stress anomalies across field sites, compare how it does across regions, and explain any single prediction.

data.text: A table of field sites by 16-day period, each row holding satellite vegetation indices, lagged and accumulated weather features, an anomaly-based stress label and the model's predicted probability, plus the raw per-site satellite time series, the saved models and their test metrics.
data.item: one field site in one 16-day period

stage.text: reviewing a trained stress-prediction model's results across sites, after training and before reporting

mechanism.text: A sidebar chooses the model and a region filter that drive every tab, and tabs show a map of each site's latest prediction, one site's history as a line chart and table, cross-region charts and tables, data-coverage counts and gap histograms, and a per-prediction attribution waterfall for a chosen site and period. Predictions are recomputed for the chosen model and cut at its tuned threshold, so every view shows the same calls as the reported metrics.

field.text: early-warning prediction of vegetation-index anomalies from satellite and weather data in remote sensing

workflow.name: review a trained classifier's predictions across sites and explain one

steps.here: The saved feature table, models and test metrics load at startup. A Model select switches between random forest and XGBoost, and the sidebar shows test accuracy, test F1 for the stress class, best CV F1 and the tuned decision threshold.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A Country select narrows the map and the site list to one region, or All.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A map shows each site's latest period as a red or green circle for predicted stress or no stress. Clicking a circle opens a popup with the period, the predicted probability and the actual label.

Choosing a site from the Location select draws its prior-period NDVI and predicted stress probability over time, with a table of the last 20 periods showing the z-score, the actual label and the predicted label.
The Country comparison tab shows stress incidence by country as bars, a per-country table of test-set metrics and the mean NDVI by calendar month for each country.

steps.step: check how complete the data is
steps.here: The Data coverage tab counts usable cloud-free composites against the number possible, draws bars of valid readings per site against that maximum, and draws a histogram of days between consecutive readings.

steps.step: explain how one result was computed
steps.here: Picking a Location and a Period draws a SHAP waterfall of the features that pushed that prediction. The final probability is set against the tuned threshold and the actual label, and log-odds are converted back to a probability for XGBoost.

distinctive: Predictions are cut at a decision threshold tuned on training data, not at 0.5, so the map and tables match the reported test metrics.
The label is an anomaly against each site's own leave-one-year-out seasonal baseline, and features come from the prior period, so predictions are made two to four weeks ahead.
Cloud gaps in the satellite record are counted against the full number of possible 16-day windows, per site and as a gap-length distribution.
The per-prediction attribution is reported in the model's own units, probability or log-odds, with a sigmoid conversion shown when needed.
The person can switch between two model families and every view recomputes.

parts.title: Model and region sidebar

parts.title: Map of latest predicted stress
